waypoints.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead (I-90 Exit 52)
waypoints.note: The Denny Creek Trail -> Hemlock Pass -> ridge -> SE talus field approach is the one used for this Southeast Slopes route.
waypoints.directions: Take I-90 to Exit 52, then follow Alpental Road to its end. Park at the Alpental day-use trailhead, at roughly 3,100 to 3,120 feet.

waypoints.name: Source Lake Trail junction
waypoints.note: Signed junction on Snow Lake Trail #1013; leave the main trail here and head toward Source Lake basin.

waypoints.name: Source Lake basin stream crossing
waypoints.note: Climbers' path fords the outlet stream draining Source Lake basin around 4,100 ft; last reliable water before the ascent gully, cairns mark the crossing.

waypoints.name: Gully 'secret passage' below the cliffs
waypoints.note: An easy-to-miss rock passage at ~4,780 ft where the route leaves the open streambed gully and climbs NE along cliff bands into the upper basin.

waypoints.name: Thumbtack (rock tower), upper basin
waypoints.note: Prominent free-standing rock tower marking the talus basin between Bryant and Chair Peak; from here the route corkscrews southwest toward the Bryant-Chair gully.

waypoints.name: Bryant-Chair Peak gully / talus shoulder
waypoints.note: Steep, loose gully between the two peaks gains a talus shoulder on Bryant's ridge; helmets recommended, rockfall risk from parties above.

waypoints.name: Summit block traverse
waypoints.note: Route stays left (south) of the talus field and traverses the south side of the west shoulder before the final scramble; exposed with loose rock, though holds are generally good.

itinerary.cal: River fords near Hardscrabble Horse Camp are safest in lower, warmer-afternoon water (July-Sept) or via an early-morning firm-snow crossing; check MBS National Forest alerts, as FS-56/Middle Fork Rd access to the Dingford Creek TH has a history of washout closures that add road-walking miles.

days.note: Drive FS-56 to the Dingford Creek/Dutch Miller Gap trailhead (check current road-closure point) and follow the Dutch Miller Gap Trail up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley — a gradual first 4.5 miles followed by a steeper final push — to a camp near Hardscrabble Horse Camp. Most parties camp here rather than pushing further, since the peak's approach begins with an unbridged river ford.
days.title: Approach to Hardscrabble camp
days.objective: Reach camp near Hardscrabble Horse Camp / the river ford

days.note: Ford the river, ascend boulder/gully terrain to about 5,200 ft, then follow the key snow gully up to the Point-5,841 pass — parties describe steep snow in the final 200-300 ft where an ice axe (and often crampons/microspikes) is needed, plus a bergschrund/moat near the top that sometimes requires dropping into the moat and traveling beneath the snow for a short stretch. From the pass it's a little over a mile of easier snow/talus to the summit; some parties tag Big Snow Mountain via the connecting ~5,760 ft pass as a bonus, but the standard plan returns straight to camp.
days.title: Burnt Boot Peak via the North Route

schedule.label: Break camp, ford the river
schedule.detail: Early crossing for firmer snow and lower water; estimated timing.

schedule.label: Ascend boulder field and gully to ~5,200 ft
schedule.detail: Mixed boulder and brush terrain below the gully proper.

schedule.label: Enter the key snow gully toward the pass
schedule.detail: Steep snow in the last 200-300 ft; ice axe required, crampons/microspikes recommended.

schedule.label: Top out at Point-5,841 pass
schedule.detail: Bergschrund/moat crossing may be needed near the top of the gully.

schedule.label: Summit Burnt Boot Peak
schedule.detail: About a mile of snow/talus travel from the pass to the summit.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the route; descending gully snow softens through the day.

days.objective: Climb Burnt Boot Peak (6,483–6,540 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and retrace the Dutch Miller Gap Trail back down to the trailhead/road.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day backpack: ~7.5 mi/~1,400 ft each way to camp near Hardscrabble Horse Camp, bookending a ~4.3-mile, ~3,600 ft round-trip summit day via the north gully.
